characters: Adoley: a fifteen-year-old JHS 3 technical designer unfolding a cardboard triangular-prism net, sharp with mensuration.
Torgbui: her classmate in heavy leather gloves and goggles using tin snips on food-grade aluminium sheet.
Fuseini: their classmate testing a colour-changing thermochromic indicator strip and cloud CSV sensor log.
Madam Kwakye: the JHS Career Technology metalwork and modern-materials teacher.

narrationPlan.voice: Clear, practical teen voices for Adoley, Torgbui, and Fuseini; encouraging Career Tech workshop voice for Madam Kwakye
narrationPlan.pace: Hands-on, exact, and inventive (about 125 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with distinct, natural voices for each JHS student and teacher.
Pause for two seconds at each comprehension check so learners can calculate or reason first.
Pronounce spreadsheet formulas, geometric terms, and security acronyms clearly and unhurriedly.

music: Crisp metallic kalimba notes with warm acoustic guitar chords conveying clean design and craftsmanship (placeholder)

teacherGuide.overview: Connects 3D prism nets, Total Surface Area, and Volume directly to building a hygienic agricultural solar dryer using non-ferrous metals, thermoplastics, NaCCA smart materials, and Computing cloud data analysis.
learningGoals: Sketch the 5-face 2D net of a triangular prism and calculate Total Surface Area and Volume.
Distinguish between aluminium, thermoplastics vs thermosets, and smart materials.
Explain safe sheet-metal deburring practices and how cloud storage supports collaboration.

beforeReading: Hold up a triangular chocolate box and cut along edges so students count 2 triangles + 3 rectangles live!
whileReading: Pause on Page 2 to highlight: (1) using 50 cm slant for top rectangle, and (2) 1 m² = 10,000 cm².
afterReading: Construct a 1 : 5 scale card model of the solar dryer net.
discussion: Why did Torgbui choose non-ferrous aluminium instead of mild steel inside a fruit dryer?
reflection: Where else could thermochromic smart materials improve safety in Ghanaian clinics or baby bottles?

mathsExtension.task: Why does 13,200 cm² equal 1.32 m² rather than 132 m²? Show the exact conversion factor.
mathsExtension.answer: 1 m = 100 cm, so 1 m² = 10,000 cm². Therefore, 13,200 cm² ÷ 10,000 = 1.32 m².

support: Colour-code each of the 5 faces on the 2D net differently so learners calculate all 5 areas.
stretch: Contrast thermoplastics with thermosetting plastics (Bakelite, melamine).
